items.title: Live Updates: Protesters March in France Amid Heavy Security
items.summary: In Marseille, clashes broke out between protesters and the police, who fired tear gas. As many as 70,000 police and security officers will try to avert the arson and looting that shocked the country last weekend.

items.title: Why Is the U.S. Accusing Canada of Election Interference?
items.summary: The Trump administration says Canadian officials are trying to sway the midterm elections for Democrats. Prime Minister Mark Carney says those claims have “no merit.”

items.title: Israel Cracks Down in West Bank City After Deadly Attack
items.summary: Hundreds of Palestinian families fled their homes as the Israeli military raided Hebron. The operation came a day after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers.

items.title: ‘Eagle’s Nest,’ Nazi-Era Guesthouse in German Alps, Is Gutted by Fire
items.summary: The police said on Saturday that the structure, a tourist attraction for decades, was probably not salvageable. A man was arrested in connection with the blaze.

items.title: Ukraine’s Feeling of Moral Whiplash at the Hands of Trump
items.summary: The United States once declared that Ukraine’s fight was the front line in a global battle for freedom. Now the Trump administration is sending money to Moscow.

items.title: Netanyahu Has Reinvented Himself. Will Voters Think It’s Enough?
items.summary: The Oct. 7 attacks marred Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s image as Mr. Security. Ahead of elections, he’s trying to sell Israelis on the new, hawkish version of himself.

items.title: Drones on Starshield Network Are Back to Normal Speeds, Ukraine Says
items.summary: The announcement followed more than a week of unexplained problems with Starshield, the Pentagon-funded satellite network Ukraine relies on to thwart Russian attacks.

items.title: Looting Left Damage and Fear on Paradise Street in Marseille
items.summary: Looters ravaged a storied commercial avenue in France’s second-largest city. Its merchants fear that more unrest could follow.

items.title: Kim Jong-un Makes First Visit to China in Over a Year
items.summary: The North Korean leader crossed the border on a newly opened bridge for the trip, as the two countries move to deepen ties.

items.title: U.S. Pressures Mexico to Deliver a Security Win Ahead of Midterm Elections
items.summary: The Trump administration wants a public victory soon, as well as a potential path to U.S. military forces in Mexico.

items.title: Noah Adams, Longtime Host of ‘All Things Considered,’ Has Died at 84
items.summary: A postman’s son from Kentucky, he worked hard to lose his accent but never forgot his Appalachian roots. “The best stories come from west of the Potomac,” he said.

items.title: C.E.O.s Say the A.I. Rollout Is Going Well. Employees Feel Differently.
items.summary: Surveys show workers and executives have different views on A.I.

items.title: Attention, Passengers: High Airfares May Be Here to Stay
items.summary: Ticket prices jumped after fuel costs spiked because of the war with Iran, but airlines say even an end to the conflict will not bring fares back down quickly.

items.title: 5 Takeaways From Our Investigation of Trump’s Waivers for Polluters
items.summary: Chemical plants and other industrial facilities had been required to curb their toxic emissions. A New York Times investigation shows how they got out of it.

items.title: How Trump Gave the Worst Polluters a Free Pass
items.summary: The president temporarily waived clean-air rules for industrial facilities that spew cancer-causing gases. Then his appointees worked to gut the regulations altogether.

items.title: France’s Avoids a Debt Downgrade From Moody’s, but Is Given a Warning
items.summary: Moody’s held the country’s credit rating steady amid political uncertainty and a rise in borrowing costs that have worsened France’s debt situation.

items.title: Ahead of Tight Race, Trump Swaps Tariffs on Some Canadian Goods
items.summary: The move was announced by Senator Susan Collins, a Maine Republican who faces a tough re-election fight amid rising prices.

items.title: Global Oil Price Hits $116 a Barrel, Highest Since April
items.summary: Investors have grown increasingly concerned that the war in Iran could escalate again, putting energy supplies at greater risk.

items.title: Why Anger About Data Centers and Energy Prices May Not Swing Votes
items.summary: In Ohio, many voters say their frustration about the increase in electricity and fuel prices and the growth of data centers won’t influence whom they vote for.

items.title: U.S. Government Takes a Cut of Chip Business in Japan-Funded Deal
items.summary: President Trump’s novel deal-making is on display in upstate New York, where the administration is funneling Japanese funds into a government-owned chip factory.

items.title: Apple’s Foldable iPhone Duo Arrives in Stores: Smartphone Review
items.summary: The first-generation Apple foldable may feel awkward, but it’s an intriguing step toward merging phones and tablets into one.

items.title: How a Legal Backlash Against Big Tech Is Forcing Big Changes
items.summary: A series of lawsuits has created a new de facto regulatory regime as courts order companies like Meta and Google to change their business practices — and pay up.

items.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
items.summary: The billionaire told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.

items.title: How the A.I. Boom Is Driving Up Sales of Gray Paint
items.summary: Tech companies are painting data centers with gray coatings on top of gray concrete and steel to resist fire, rust and static electricity. That has made data centers a fast-growing market for paint makers.

items.title: What’s the Deal With Billy Evans? A Spoiler-Filled Guide to ‘You Can See Everything’
items.summary: “You shouldn’t overbeat scrambled eggs.”

items.title: What Is PHP? Why Are Government and Business Websites Going Offline?
items.summary: A critical security flaw in the programming language underpinning much of the web has prompted a global rush to patch vulnerable systems.

items.summary: Governments and businesses around the world scrambled to prevent hackers from exploiting a vulnerability in PHP, a popular programming language.

items.title: Anthropic Joins the A.I. Agent Race With Claude Duet
items.summary: The tool, which is not yet widely available, will compete with OpenAI’s dots and Meta’s Muse. It is built for work and not personal errands.

items.title: Meta Earnings Show Increased A.I. Spending, Even as Cash Pressures Grow
items.summary: The spending has hurt the Silicon Valley giant’s cash flow, which turned negative. Meta said it would issue a new class of stock to help it raise more money.
